actual_tools: Life Sciences Databases public API evidence and allele-resolved JSON aggregation
execution.implementation: retained ClinVar, Ensembl, and UKB-TOPMed allele-specific observations plus a genuine Rosalind task-chooser observation

observations: ClinVar returned distinct C>T and C>G records for rs7903146; the selected C>T allele is Variation ID 7413.
Ensembl returned rs7903146 cross-references including VCV000007413.
UKB-TOPMed reported allele frequency 0.29 and 1,419 available association rows for 10:112998590-C-T.
The verified gnomAD r4 query returned genome AC 41622, AN 151914, and AF 0.2739839646 for the C>T allele.
The Rosalind launcher returned ready=true and did not execute a scientific job.
interpretation: The case demonstrates allele-resolved identity checking before combining clinical, annotation, and cohort records.
limitations: The compact ClinVar search is not a complete clinical-significance review.
The first UKB-TOPMed slice is not significance-ranked.
Population frequency is not a clinical classification, and the explicit C>T allele must be preserved across services.
An rsID-only UKB-TOPMed lookup selected C>G; only the explicit GRCh38 C>T result is used as evidence.

provenance.note: Exact public accessions and query parameters are retained in outputs/provenance.json; outputs/rosalind-open-observation.json records the genuine launcher call and states that no scientific job executed.

reproduction: Repeat the ClinVar, Ensembl, explicit GRCh38 C>T UKB-TOPMed, and gnomAD r4 requests in outputs/query-verification.json.
Keep the C>T and C>G ClinVar records separate and avoid rsID-only allele resolution for UKB-TOPMed.
Compare outputs/results.json and the preview with the allele-resolved query summaries.
